title: Day 606 — CNTE Sección 22 Extraordinary Assembly Formally Votes to Join June 1 National Strike; Section Leader Declares Core Demands Unmet
detail: On May 30, 2026 (Day 606 — a Saturday with no mañanera), the CNTE's Sección 22 (Oaxaca teachers' section, the union's largest with approximately 70,000 members) convened an extraordinary state assembly in Oaxaca city to evaluate the outcomes of three rounds of dialogue with the federal government (Secretaría de Gobernación, SEP) and determine next steps. ASSEMBLY OUTCOME: Section leader Yenny Aracely Pérez addressed the assembly and declared that while the government had provided partial responses on administrative matters (payroll corrections, housing fund review), the core demands remained unmet: (1) Abrogation of the 2007 ISSSTE pension reform; (2) 100% base salary raise; (3) Reinstatement of workers dismissed under the 2019 Education Reform teacher evaluation system. The extraordinary assembly formally voted to: (a) Join the national indefinite strike call beginning June 1, 2026; (b) Suspend all school operations statewide from June 1 until demands are met; (c) Support the national mega-march to be held in Mexico City on June 1 with participation from Sección 22's delegados. Pérez stated the government had shown 'cerrazón' (closed-mindedness) on the central demands. BROADER CNTE CONTEXT: Sección 7 (Chiapas), Sección 18 (Michoacán), and sections from Guerrero and Hidalgo had already announced solidarity actions for June 1. The strike and march were deliberately timed to coincide with the FIFA World Cup 2026 opening weekend (Mexico vs. South Africa, June 11 at Estadio Azteca) to maximize international visibility pressure on the government.

media.caption: CNTE Sección 22 (Oaxaca) extraordinary assembly votes to join June 1 national strike — section leader Yenny Pérez declares core pension and salary demands remain unmet after three rounds of SEGOB talks

title: Day 606 — Morena Formally Convokes Nationwide Mobilization for May 31 Government Report at Monumento a la Revolución
detail: On May 30, 2026 (Day 606), Morena's national leadership — under newly elected National President Ariadna Montiel Reyes (elected May 3–4) — formally issued a nationwide mobilization convocation for supporters to accompany President Claudia Sheinbaum at the Monumento a la Revolución public gathering on May 31 at 10:00 AM. The mobilization was framed as a 'defense of sovereignty and celebration of the Fourth Transformation's second year.' Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada had previously called a mass mobilization at the monument for 9:00 AM (one hour before Sheinbaum's live address from the National Palace). The gathering at the Monumento a la Revolución esplanade in Colonia Tabacalera was expected to draw tens of thousands, with supporters arriving from across the country via organized transportation arranged by Morena's territorial structures in all 32 states. Simultaneously, the government confirmed that public screens would broadcast the report live at plazas, cultural centers, and government spaces across all 32 state capitals. The Zócalo was unavailable as the FIFA World Cup Fan Fest installation was underway ahead of the June 11 opening match (Mexico vs. South Africa). The accountability report, titled 'En Defensa de la Soberanía' (In Defense of Sovereignty), would mark approximately two years since Sheinbaum's June 2, 2024 electoral victory with 59.76% of the vote.

media.caption: Morena officially convokes May 31 mobilization at Monumento a la Revolución — Ariadna Montiel's first major national convocation as Morena National President; Clara Brugada calls supporters from 9 AM
